proposals.expected_failure_mode: If admissions systematically lag infections, delay=0 will shift peaks early and degrade fit around turning points.
proposals.rationale: Primary SEIRS family with fractional dynamics; tests whether this hospitalization-rate series aligns closely with contemporaneous infections (no lag) while keeping structure consistent with prior best.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May underperform if the effective lag varies over time or differs by season, leading to residual phase error.
proposals.rationale: Replicates the previous best specification to anchor comparisons and isolate the effect of alternative delays on forecast stability.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is closer to 1 week, delay=2 can over-lag the signal, smoothing/late-peaking forecasts and increasing split-to-split variability.
proposals.rationale: Same fractional SEIRS with a slightly longer lag to test sensitivity in the narrow 0–2 week neighborhood while preserving parsimony.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Reduced robustness and higher variability across splits; may struggle to capture moderate peakiness at high rate scale without fractional memory effects.
proposals.rationale: Single non-fractional robustness comparator matched to the best delay; checks whether fractional dynamics are essential versus a standard SEIRS with the same observation timing.
